items.title: Dataset and index updates
items.text: For dataset and index updates, distinguish the training objective from the evaluation goal. Check provenance and data quality, keep validation/test examples isolated from training, record the baseline and configuration, and evaluate both improvement on the target task and possible regressions elsewhere.

items.title: Dependency and security updates
items.text: Dependency and security updates is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

items.title: Monitoring model behavior changes
items.text: Use monitoring model behavior changes to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

items.title: User feedback and issue resolution
items.text: User feedback and issue resolution connects model capabilities to a real user's task. Define an observable success measure, keep uncertainty and failure states visible, make correction or escalation possible, and compare the AI-assisted workflow with a useful baseline rather than optimizing engagement alone.

items.title: Long-term maintenance planning
items.text: Long-term maintenance planning describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice model deprecation and provider changes within maintaining ai systems: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
